accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: William Foster — Six Voyages
Tapan Raychaudhuri — Co-editor of the Cambridge Economic History of India, Volume I
Tavernier — The Agrarian System of Mughal India, 1556-1707
W.H. Moreland — Storia do Mogor
accepted.x: Tapan Raychaudhuri was a co-editor, along with Irfan Habib, of the Cambridge Economic History of India, Volume I. Six Voyages was associated with Tavernier, Early Travels in India with William Foster, and Storia do Mogor with Niccolao Manucci.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work association and reject swapped authorship traps.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: Which of the following works is associated with J.B. Tavernier?
o: Travels in the Mogul Empire
Six Voyages
India at the Death of Akbar
Early Travels in India, 1583-1619
accepted.x: J.B. Tavernier wrote Six Voyages, also referred to as Six Travels in India. The other works were associated with Bernier, William Foster and W.H. Moreland respectively.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely related travel accounts by matching the traveller with the exact title.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Francois Bernier:
1. He was a French physician.
2. He served as the physician of Dara Shikoh.
3. He was patronised by Danishmand Khan.
4. He argued that the absence of private property in land contributed to agrarian ruin.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Bernier was a French physician, served Dara Shikoh, was patronised by Danishmand Khan, and linked the absence of private landownership with agrarian deterioration.
accepted.tq: Check each biographical and analytical detail separately before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: Bernier's observations on the Mughal economy included which one of the following combinations?
o: Private ownership of all land, agrarian prosperity and outflow of precious metals
Imperial ownership of land, agrarian ruin, inflow of precious metals and prosperity of merchants
Village ownership of land, decline of trade and absence of merchants
Merchant ownership of land, peasant prosperity and exclusive use of copper currency
accepted.x: Bernier believed that the emperor owned all land and blamed this arrangement for agrarian ruin. He nevertheless acknowledged that precious metals flowed into India and that merchants prospered.
accepted.tq: Separate the traveller's criticism of landholding from his observations on trade and precious-metal inflow.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: J.B. Tavernier was best known in the context of Mughal-period India as a
o: Dutch VOC merchant who spent seven years in Agra
English merchant who recorded a famine during Shah Jahan's reign
French diamond merchant who visited the diamond mines of Golconda
French physician who served Dara Shikoh
accepted.x: Tavernier was a French gem and diamond merchant who made six visits to India and described the diamond mines of Golconda. The other descriptions relate to Bernier, Pelsaert and Peter Mundy.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among European visitors by identifying profession and subject of observation.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding Tavernier is correct?
o: He reached Surat in 1666 and visited the Qutb Shahi tombs.
He was an Italian doctor who wrote Storia do Mogor.
He visited India only once during Akbar's reign.
He made six visits and recorded the Koh-i-Noor from the Kollur mines.
accepted.x: Tavernier made six visits to India during the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb and documented the Koh-i-Noor associated with the Kollur mines. The other options describe Manucci or Thevenot, or give an incorrect number and period of visits.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail and compare the traveller's identity with nearby European visitors.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: The Koh-i-Noor recorded by Tavernier was associated with which of the following?
o: The Golconda mines in Hyderabad and a weight of 40 carats
The Surat mines and a weight of 165 carats
The Kollur diamond mines in Guntur and a weight of 106 carats
The Agra mines and a weight of 178 grains
accepted.x: Tavernier recorded the Koh-i-Noor as a 106-carat diamond from the Kollur mines in Guntur. The other locations and measurements are not associated with this description.
accepted.tq: Combine the place and figure to avoid confusion between diamond details and coin weights.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Traveller)
A. Niccolao Manucci
B. Jean de Thevenot
C. Francisco Pelsaert
D. Peter Mundy

List-II (Description)
1. Dutch VOC merchant who came in 1620 and stayed seven years in Agra
2. English merchant who recorded a famine during Shah Jahan's reign
3. Italian doctor associated with the Mughal court and court intrigues after Shah Jahan
4. French traveller and physician who reached Surat in 1666

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Manucci was the Italian doctor linked with court intrigues; Thevenot reached Surat in 1666; Pelsaert was the Dutch VOC merchant; and Peter Mundy was the English merchant who recorded a famine.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive nationality or profession and then complete the matching code.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: Jean de Thevenot's travels in India included visits to
o: Lahore, Kabul and Bengal only
Guntur, Bijapur and Fatehpur Sikri
Surat, Machilipatnam and Golconda
Agra, Kollur and Delhi only
accepted.x: Jean de Thevenot, a French traveller and physician, reached Surat in 1666 and visited Machilipatnam and Golconda. His account also referred to Hyderabad and the Qutb Shahi tombs.
accepted.tq: Use the travel itinerary as a location-based discrimination question.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Sir Thomas Roe reached Jahangir's court.
B. Francisco Pelsaert came to India.
C. Peter Mundy travelled in India.
D. Jean de Thevenot reached Surat.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: A, B, C, D
B, A, C, D
A, C, B, D
B, C, A, D
accepted.x: Sir Thomas Roe reached Jahangir's court in 1615, Pelsaert came in 1620, Peter Mundy travelled during 1630-34, and Thevenot reached Surat in 1666.
accepted.tq: Place the dated events first and then arrange the intervening travel accounts.
accepted.sec: Historians and travellers on the Mughal economy - books

accepted.s: Captain William Hawkins and Sir Thomas Roe are respectively associated with
o: Shah Jahan's reign at Agra and Aurangzeb's court in 1666
Akbar's reign at Fatehpur Sikri and Shah Jahan's court in 1630
Jahangir's reign at Surat and Jahangir's court in 1615
Aurangzeb's reign at Golconda and Jahangir's court in 1605
accepted.x: Captain William Hawkins came to Surat during Jahangir's reign, while Sir Thomas Roe visited Jahangir's court in 1615. The other combinations incorrectly assign their periods or locations.
accepted.tq: Distinguish two English visitors by pairing each with the correct Mughal setting and date.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Dam — Copper
Mohur — Gold
Rupiya — Silver
Chalni — Coins of a previous reign accepted at a discount
accepted.x: Chalni referred to coins of the current reign in circulation. Coins of a previous reign accepted at a discount were called Khazana.
accepted.tq: Find the one reversed definition among the coin-metal and coin-status pairs.

accepted.s:
With reference to Mughal coinage, consider the following statements:
1. The rupiya was a silver coin standardised by Sher Shah.
2. Sher Shah's rupiya weighed 178 grains.
3. Akbar continued the silver rupiya standard.
4. The dam was a copper coin.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The silver rupiya was standardised by Sher Shah at 178 grains, continued by Akbar, while the dam was made of copper.
accepted.tq: Combine the metal, standardiser, weight and continuation details before choosing the coded option.

accepted.s: How many dams were equivalent to one rupee in the Mughal monetary system?
accepted.x: Forty copper dams were equivalent to one rupee. The dam was the copper denomination, while the rupiya was the silver coin.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact conversion figure rather than confusing it with the coin's metal or name.

accepted.s: The term 'Sikka' in the Mughal monetary system denoted
o: the copper coin equal to one-fortieth of a rupee
the gold coin used for long-distance trade
coins of a previous reign accepted at a discount
the right of coinage in the ruler's name, signifying sovereignty along with the khutba
accepted.x: Sikka denoted the right of coinage in the ruler's name and, together with the khutba, symbolised sovereignty. The other options describe the dam, khazana and mohur respectively.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a political symbol of sovereignty from the names of actual coin denominations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about coin circulation in the Deccan is correct?
o: Golconda minted only silver coins and prohibited copper currency.
Mughal silver coins circulated even in Golconda, while Golconda itself minted only copper coins.
Golconda circulated only gold coins and rejected Mughal silver coins.
Mughal coins circulated only in northern India and not in Golconda.
accepted.x: Mughal silver coins circulated in Golconda, although Golconda itself minted only copper coins, as noted by Thevenot.
accepted.tq: Use the contrast between circulation and local minting to reject reversed regional claims.
